newsitem.title: INDIA: End account trade pulls Bombay shares down.
newsitem.headline: End account trade pulls Bombay shares down.

text.p: Share prices ended lower on Friday largely on sales prompted by end-account trade on the Bombay Stock Stock Exchange (BSE), dealers said.
"On both exchanges, positions are overbought," Antony Sequeira, managing director of Arcadia Share & Stock Brokers said about the BSE and the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The Bombay-30-share index closed 57.23 points or 1.31 percent lower at a provisional 4,321.14.
The NSE index closed 12.35 points or one percent down at a provisional 1,223 points.
Squaring operations pulled down the shares, traders said.
They expected the downtrend to continue till Tuesday, the last day of account on the NSE. Prices should pick up beginning Wednesday as foreign fund buying continued, they said.
Select Indian blue-chips bucked the trend to post gains.
The list included HDFC which rose 257 rupees to 4,760 on the BSE, Infosys by 183 rupees to 2,450, NIIT by 30.50 rupees to 460.50 and Indian Hume Pipes by 39 rupees to 439.
Larsen & Toubro and Tata Tea, which accounted for the top volumes on the BSE, also rose marginally on Friday.
Reliance, State Bank, Tata Steel, TELCO, ICICI, ITC and MTNL, which accounted for the bulk of trade on the BSE, lost marginally.
Some traders said Friday's correction was welcome.
"The short-term correction is healthy for the market," said Govind Agarwal, head of sales at brokerage Motilal Oswal Securities.
Anand Jhaveri, head of broking at Birla Marlin Securities, said the BSE index could dip to 4,000-level.
"The immediate top would be 4,500," he said. The index had touched an all-time high of 4,643.31 points in September 1994.
